description: Figure 2 displays five grouped bar charts, each illustrating a distinct layer grouping pattern across four groups labeled G₁ through G₄ along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis represents the number of layers in each group, with bars extending upward to indicate this count. The five patterns shown are labeled beneath their respective charts as “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck.” In the “Increasing” pattern, the bar heights rise progressively from left to right. The “Uniform” pattern shows four bars of equal height. The “Decreasing” pattern features bars that progressively shorten from left to right. The “Spindle” pattern has shorter bars at the ends (G₁ and G₄) and taller bars in the middle (G₂ and G₃). The “Bottleneck” pattern shows tall bars at the ends (G₁ and G₄) and shorter bars in the middle (G₂ and G₃). All bars are rendered in a light green color, and the chart does not include any numerical scale or tick marks on the vertical axis. The bars are not sorted by height and are presented in the order of their respective labels.
